'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations]]
****[[2026 Iran war ceasefire]]
*****After pressure from the [[United States]], [[Israel]] agrees to hold direct talks with [[Lebanon]] in [[Washington, D.C.]], but refuses to observe the Iran war [[ceasefire]] in Lebanon. [https://english.news.cn/europe/20260409/76c8e2ea04894d5290bfb2256c3f886f/c.html (Xinhua)]
*****[[President of Iran|Iranian president]] [[Masoud Pezeshkian]] says that [[Supreme Leader of Iran|supreme leader]] [[Mojtaba Khamenei]] had approved the ceasefire. ***[[2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries]]
****[[2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain]]
*****The [[Bahrain Defence Force|Bahraini military]] intercepts seven [[Unmanned aerial vehicles in the Iranian military|drones from Iran]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/bahrain-reports-new-drone-attack-from-iran-on-2nd-day-of-ceasefire/3899405 (AA)]

***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****The [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy]] announces alternative routes for ships crossing the [[Strait of Hormuz]], citing risks of [[Naval mine|sea mines]] in the main shipping channel. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2639281/middle-east (AFP via Arab News)]
****[[Abu Dhabi National Oil Company]] [[Chief executive officer|CEO]] [[Sultan Al Jaber]] says that the strait is still not open because Iran has been restricting and controlling traffic. [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/09/iran-war-oil-strait-hormuz-tanker-ship-uae.html (CNBC)]
****[[Gabon]]-flagged [[oil tanker]] ''MSG'' crosses the [[Strait of Hormuz]] according to [[MarineTraffic]], making it the first non-Iranian oil tanker to cross the [[waterway]] since the ceasefire was announced. [https://www.gulftoday.ae/news/2026/04/09/first-non-iranian-tanker-transits-strait-of-hormuz-since-ceasefire (''Gulf Today'')]
***[[List of Iranian officials killed during the 2026 Iran war|Iranian officials killed during the 2026 Iran war]]
****Former [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Iran)|Iranian foreign minister]] [[Kamal Kharazi]] dies from injuries sustained during an Israeli–U.S. airstrike on his home on April 1. [https://www.ynetnews.com/article/62ohmrssa (Ynet)]
**[[Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)|Hezbollah–Israel conflict]]
***[[2026 Lebanon war]]
****[[Hezbollah]] launches [[Hezbollah armed strength#Rockets|rockets]] at the [[Israel]]i [[kibbutz]] of [[Manara, Israel|Manara]], citing Israeli and American violations of the ceasefire linked to the Iran war. [https://www.abs-cbn.com/news/world/2026/4/9/hezbollah-says-fired-rockets-towards-israel-in-response-to-violation-of-ceasefire-1022 (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]
****At least seven people are killed by a wave of Israeli [[airstrike]]s and [[artillery]] [[Shell (projectile)|shelling]] across [[Lebanon]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/4/9/fresh-israeli-attacks-on-lebanon-threaten-us-iran-ceasefire (Al Jazeera)]
****The [[Israeli Defense Forces|Israeli military]] says that it has killed [[Lebanese Resistance Brigades]] commanders Maher Qassem Hamdan and Ali Yusuf Harshi, personal secretary and nephew of [[Secretary-General of Hezbollah|Hezbollah leader]] [[Naim Qassem]]. [https://www.jpost.com/middle-east/article-892427 (''The Jerusalem Post'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israeli-military-says-it-has-killed-nephew-hezbollah-chief-naim-qassem-2026-04-09/ (Reuters)]
****Hezbollah says that its fighters are engaged in "[[Close quarters battle|point-blank clashes]]" with [[Israeli Ground Forces|Israeli troops]] in [[Bint Jbeil]], Lebanon. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2026/04/09/hezbollah-says-engaging-israeli-forces-directly-in-south-lebanon-town-of-bint-jbeil (''Al Arabiya'')] 
****[[Government of Lebanon|Lebanese authorities]] update the losses from the [[8 April 2026 Lebanon attacks|previous day's attacks]] to 303 killed and 1,150 injured. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/death-toll-from-wednesday-s-israeli-strikes-in-lebanon-rises-to-303-health-ministry/3900136 (AA)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Russia–United Kingdom relations]], [[Russian sabotage operations in Europe]]
***[[Secretary of State for Defence|British defence secretary]] [[John Healey]] says three [[Russian Navy]] submarines engaged in [[covert operation]]s against the UK in the [[North Sea]] near its [[European Union submarine internet cables|undersea cables]] and says counter-measures are underway. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/cg54mdlqppjt (BBC News)]
**The [[Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War]] says that [[Russia]] has returned 1,000 bodies of fallen individuals to [[Ukraine]] as part of repatriation efforts. [https://en.interfax.com.ua/news/general/1158030.html (Interfax Ukraine)]
**[[President of Russia|Russian president]] [[Vladimir Putin]] declares a ceasefire for the weekend in Ukraine for [[Easter|Orthodox Easter]]. [https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-putin-orthodox-easter-ceasefire-ff25a818f5509d6820df1f3deba587e7 (AP)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Darfur campaign (2023–present)|Darfur campaign]]
***The [[Sudan Founding Alliance]] says that over 56 civilians, including 17 children, are killed and 107 are injured in a [[Sudanese Armed Forces|Sudanese]] [[drone warfare|drone strike]] on a wedding celebration in [[Kutum]], [[North Darfur]], [[Sudan]]. [https://thesudantimes.com/sudan/tasis-56-civilians-killed-in-saf-drone-strike-on-wedding-in-darfur/ (''The Sudan Times'')]

[https://sudantribune.com/article/312613 (''Sudan Tribune'')] [https://sudanhorizon.com/wfp-sudan-country-office-returns-to-khartoum-after-three-years/ (Sudan Horizon)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war]]
**The [[European Bank for Reconstruction and Development]] announces plans to allocate [[Euro|€]]5 billion to support economies affected by the Iran war, focusing on [[financial system]]s, businesses, and infrastructure in [[Egypt]], [[Iraq]], [[Jordan]], and [[Lebanon]]. [https://www.lse.co.uk/news/ebrd-to-deploy-5-billion-euros-in-countries-hit-by-iran-war-xolgni9ibt6tlfr.html (Reuters via London South East)]
**[[Gulf Air]], the [[flag carrier]] of [[Bahrain]], announces a plan to return its operations hub to [[Bahrain International Airport]] after having relocated to [[King Fahd International Airport]] in [[Dammam]], [[Saudi Arabia]], during the Iran war. [https://aerospaceglobalnews.com/news/gulf-air-return-bahrain-iran-ceasefire/ (Aerospace Global News)]
**[[Price of oil|Oil prices]] rebound amidst concerns about the ceasefire, with [[Petroleum in the United States|U.S.]] and [[Brent Crude]] oil back up to nearly [[United States dollar|US$]]100 per [[Barrel (unit)|barrel]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/business/energy/oil-prices-iran-ceasefire-doubts-rcna267421 (NBC News)]
**[[Saudi Arabia]] reports that the recent Iranian attack on a [[pumping station]] of the [[East–West Crude Oil Pipeline]] reduced its throughput by  700,000 barrels per day. [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/09/iran-war-oil-saudi-arabia-east-west-pipeline.html (CNBC)]
*[[Mining in Venezuela]]
**[[Venezuela]]'s [[National Assembly of Venezuela|National Assembly]] approves a reform of mining laws that allows greater private investment in the country's mineral sector, with the bill advancing to [[Constitution of Venezuela|constitutional]] review. The measure forms part of broader economic changes aimed at increasing foreign participation in natural resource industries. [https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2026/04/10/venezuelan-lawmakers-approve-sweeping-mining-bill-to-lure-foreign-investors_6752277_4.html (''Le Monde'')]
*[[USAID in the second Trump administration]]
**The [[OECD]] reports that [[official development assistance]] from its member states declined by 23.1 percent in real terms to US$174.3 billion, marking the largest recorded annual decrease, with the reduction largely driven by cuts from the [[United States foreign aid|United States]]. [https://www.indopremier.com/ipotnews/newsDetail.php?jdl=Development_aid_down__historic__23_1_percent_in_2025__OECD&news_id=1726284&group_news=ALLNEWS&taging_subtype=UNITEDSTATES&name=&search=y_general&q=UNITED%20STATES,%20&halaman=1 (AFP via Indo Premier)]
